paragraphs: R. Chama son of Rabbi Chanina: Berakhot 15b, near the end, two statements; Beitzah 16a; Niddah 71a. Taanit 7a has “R. Chama said: R. Chanina said: What does ‘Iron sharpens iron’ mean?” It should read “R. Chama bar Chanina said”; so too in Ein Yaakov. Sanhedrin 35a: “Whence these matters? R. Chama bar Chanina said”; so too in Ein Yaakov. Taanit 25a, near the end: R. Chama bar Chanina decreed a fast, but rain did not come. They said, “But R. Yehoshua ben Levi decreed a fast, and rain came!” He answered, “Here am I, and here is the son of Levi”—Rashi explains: he is superior to me—etc. They prayed, but rain did not come, etc. He said, “Firmament, cover your face!” It did not cover. He said, “How brazen is the firmament's face!” It covered with clouds, and rain came. A similar matter in the Jerusalem Talmud concerns the unqualified R. Chanina, who is bar Chama, with R. Yehoshua ben Levi; see there. Shabbat 147b: R. Chama bar Chanina and R. Yochanan; see R. Yosi bar Chanina and what I wrote there. R. Berekhiah, in his name. With R. Hoshaya: end of Peah. “I heard it from R. Chiyya bar Abba's lecture”—Sanhedrin 29a. “R. Yitzchak said”—Berakhot. R. Levi, in his name: Bereshit Rabbah, sections 20, Vayetze 68, Vayeshev 84; Acharei Mot, section 20. R. Levi bar Chama, in his name: Zevachim 53b, near the end; they disagree at the beginning of chapter 2 of Taanit. Or Levi bar Lachma said: R. Chama bar Chanina—Rosh Hashanah 29b. Rabbi lodged together with him: Shabbat 38a, near the end. This requires investigation, since his father, Rabbi Chanina, presided after Rabbi's death. R. Shmuel bar Natan, in his name.
